text: every closed C^r 1-form on a simply connected manifold is the differential of a C^r function, so H¹_dR vanishes (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, Ch. 11).

name: Semisimple linear Lie algebras contain the Jordan parts of their elements
text: a semisimple Lie subalgebra of 𝔤𝔩(V) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero contains the semisimple and nilpotent parts of each element, so faithful representations preserve the abstract Jordan decomposition (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras*, §6.4).

name: The dual Jacobi–Trudi identity
text: s_μ = det(e_{μ′ᵢ − i + j}) in the elementary symmetric polynomials over any commutative ring, the half left open when the Jacobi–Trudi identity was announced (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I (3.5)).

name: Symplectic transvections generate the symplectic group
text: over every field, in any characteristic, the symplectic transvections generate Sp_{2m}(K) (Artin, *Geometric Algebra*, Ch. III).

name: Topological generators of tori
text: every compact connected abelian Lie group has an element generating a dense subgroup, and such generators form a dense set (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, I.4.14).

name: Lakshmibai–Seshadri paths
text: Littelmann's encoding of the LS paths of shape λ by decreasing chains of Weyl-group cosets and rational times satisfying the a-chain condition, finitely many for each λ (Littelmann, *Invent. Math.* 116 (1994)).

name: Killing vector fields
text: vector fields X with L_X g = 0, characterised by skew-adjointness of ∇X, with ∇²X = R(·, X)· and the restriction of X to any geodesic a Jacobi field (Petersen, *Riemannian Geometry*, Ch. 8).

name: Stable distributions
text: the probability laws on ℝ with the stable characteristic function of index α ∈ (0, 2], skewness |β| ≤ 1, scale and location, in Nolan's S₀ parametrisation (Nolan, *Univariate Stable Distributions*, Ch. 1).

name: Borel–Moore homology
text: the homology of locally finite singular chains with local coefficients, agreeing with ordinary homology on compact spaces (Bredon, *Sheaf Theory*, Ch. V).

name: The affine Weyl group
text: the group generated by the affine reflections s_{α,k} of a root pairing, whose elements are exactly the affine maps with linear part in W and translation in the coroot lattice, W_aff = Q^∨ ⋊ W (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §4.2).

name: The group Spinᶜ
text: Spinᶜ(Q) = (Spin(Q) × U(1))/{±1}, with its determinant map to U(1) and its map to SO(Q), the kernel of their product being of order two (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, App. D).

name: The fundamental group of a graph of groups
text: Serre's π₁(𝔸, T): the free product of the vertex groups and the free group on the edges, modulo the edge relations and the edges of T (Serre, *Trees*, I §5.1).

name: Hirzebruch's multiplicative sequences
text: the polynomials K_k in the elementary symmetric functions with Σ K_k = ∏ Q(xᵢ) for a power series Q, multiplicative on disjoint unions of roots (Hirzebruch, *Topological Methods in Algebraic Geometry*, §1).

name: The Turing jump
text: Z′ = {e : the e-th Z-computable program halts on input e}, with Z <_T Z′ and every Z-c.e. set one-one reducible to Z′ (Soare, *Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degrees*, III.2).

name: The lemniscate constant
text: ϖ = 2∫₀¹ dt/√(1 − t⁴), the half-length of the lemniscate, with the closed form ϖ = Γ(1/4)²/(2√(2π)) (Borwein–Borwein, *Pi and the AGM*, Ch. 1).
Correctly stated: every finite abelian extension of ℚ embeds in some ℚ(ζₙ), n ≠ 0 (Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, Thm 14.1; Wikipedia); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: π_{n+1}(Γ K, 0) ≃ H_{n+1}(K) for a nonnegatively graded chain complex of R-modules, natural in chain maps (Goerss–Jardine, Simplicial Homotopy Theory, Cor. III.2.7); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: π₀(Γ K) ≃ H₀(K) (Goerss–Jardine III.2.7); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: with [1], …, [n] units, the unique idempotent of augmentation 1 killed on both sides by every eᵢ, the Jones–Wenzl projection (Wenzl 1987; Kauffman–Lins, Temperley–Lieb Recoupling Theory, Ch. 3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: for p + q ≥ 2 the image of Spin(p, q) → SO(p, q) is the identity component SO₀(p, q) (Lawson–Michelsohn, Spin Geometry, I §2; Wikipedia, Spin group, indefinite signature); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: over an algebraically closed field, G / R_u(G) is a torus for a reduced connected solvable affine group of finite type (Borel, Linear Algebraic Groups, Thm 10.6(1); Humphreys 19.3(a)); the docstring claims no splitting G = T ⋉ G_u; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: in the Black–Scholes market with physical drift μ, callValue at S_u equals e^{−r(T−u)} E_Q[(S_T − K)⁺ | ℱ_u] Q-a.s. under the Girsanov-tilted risk-neutral measure (Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance II, §§5.2.4–5.2.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: on a closed manifold, PSC metrics joined by a path of PSC metrics continuous in the chart C² topology are concordant (Gromov–Lawson, Ann. of Math. 111 (1980), Lemma 3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Newton above Hodge for a matrix with a Smith normal form over a ring with a nonnegative valuation, finite v(det A) (Kedlaya, A little p-adic numerical analysis, §3 Thm 16); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: the slope-data form of Newton above Hodge (Kedlaya, A little p-adic numerical analysis, §3 Thm 16); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: the Newton polygon of det(1 − XA) at n is Σ v(sᵢ), the Hodge endpoint (Kedlaya, §3 Thm 16); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: κ(G) ≤ λ(G) for every simple graph, Whitney's inequality (Diestel, Graph Theory, Prop. 1.4.2; Whitney 1932); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: PGL(2, K) is sharply 3-transitive on P¹(K), normalised at (0, 1, ∞) (Wikipedia, Projective linear group; Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, Ch. 3 §3.3 for K = ℂ); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the three roots of (X + 16)³ − jX are the twelfth powers of the level-two Siegel functions, Weber's identities (𝔣²⁴ − 16)³ = j𝔣²⁴, (𝔣ᵢ²⁴ + 16)³ = j𝔣ᵢ²⁴ in Siegel-function form (Wikipedia, Weber modular function; Cox, Primes of the Form x² + ny², §12); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the nuclear operators E → F with the nuclear norm, the quotient of E* ⊗̂π F by the kernel of the canonical map (Ryan, Introduction to Tensor Products of Banach Spaces, Ch. 2); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: B ⊆ A whose leading terms generate the initial algebra of A (Robbiano–Sweedler 1990; Sturmfels, Gröbner Bases and Convex Polytopes, Ch. 11); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the group presented on simple classes by [S][T] = [U] whenever Hom(U, S ⊗ T) ≠ 0, the universal grading group (EGNO, Tensor Categories, §4.14); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: some resolvent is a compact operator, equivalently every one (Kato, Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators, III §6.8; Reed–Simon IV, XIII.14); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: chart-locally induced by an adic morphism of Huber pairs (Huber, Math. Z. 217 (1994), §3), with the analytic-points characterisation Prop. 3.2(ii); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: H^k_c(E) = 0 for k ≠ dim E on a finite-dimensional real normed space, the vanishing half of the Poincaré lemma for compact supports (Bott–Tu, §4; Lee, Thm 17.28); the top degree is a separate statement, as the docstring says; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Grothendieck's inequality for bounded bilinear forms on C(K) × C(L) with the constant 16, not sharp, as the docstring says (Albiac–Kalton, Topics in Banach Space Theory, 8.1.3); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: Menger's theorem, internally vertex-disjoint paths, for multigraphs with finitely many vertices (Menger 1927; Schrijver, Combinatorial Optimization, §9.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: the undirected max-flow/min-cut theorem for nonnegative edge capacities on a multigraph (Ford–Fulkerson, Flows in Networks, Ch. I); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the Littlewood–Richardson rule with c^ν_{λμ} the number of Littlewood–Richardson tableaux of shape ν/λ and content μ (Fulton, Young Tableaux, §5.1); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the Littlewood–Richardson rule for rational Weyl modules of GLₙ(ℂ) indexed by arbitrary dominant weights, via determinant twists (Fulton–Harris, Lecture 6 and §15.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
Correctly stated: flasque sheaves of modules have Extⁿ⁺¹(R_U, F) = 0, so are acyclic (Hartshorne, Prop. III.2.5); compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the stable category of Gorenstein-projective objects of an abelian category embeds fully faithfully into D^b(C)/Perf(C) (X.-W. Chen, Math. Nachr. 284 (2011), Thm 2.1); the docstring claims only the fully faithful half of Buchweitz; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.

Correctly stated: the lattice glued from a row of the rootful rank-24 table along its glue code (Conway–Sloane, SPLAG, Ch. 16 §1, Table 16.1); unimodularity is proved for 19 rows and labelled so; compared in Voyager's full-statement test.
